items.title: Section: Why the Body Still Feels Something Even in Deep Meditation, and Why Cessation Never Truly Empties the Body of Mind

items.zh: 何故若無阿賴耶識，身受差別不應道理？謂如有一，或如理思，或不如理；或無思慮，或隨尋伺；或處定心，或不在定；爾時於身諸領受起非一眾多種種差別，彼應無有。然現可得，是故定有阿賴耶識。何故若無阿賴耶識，處無心定不應道理？謂入無想定、或滅盡定，應如捨命識，離於身，非不離身。如世尊說：當於爾時，識不離身故。
items.en:
Sixth, differences in bodily sensation; first, posing the question. Why, apart from the store-consciousness, do differences in bodily sensation fail to make sense?
Second, explaining; first, arguing there would be none. Whether reflecting correctly or incorrectly, without deliberation, engaged in coarse or subtle examination, in concentration or not, the body gives rise to a whole range of distinct sensations at that time; apart from the store-consciousness, there ought to be none.
Second, concluding it definitely exists. Yet such sensation is indeed found to occur; therefore the store-consciousness definitely exists.
Seventh, abiding in mindless concentration; first, posing the question. Why, apart from the store-consciousness, does abiding in mindless concentration fail to make sense?
Second, explaining; first, arguing the fault. Entering the attainment without perception or the attainment of cessation ought to be like dying, consciousness departing the body — yet it does not depart the body.
Second, citing proof. As the Blessed One said: at that very time, consciousness does not depart from the body.

items.zh: 何故若無阿賴耶識，命終時識不應道理？

items.title: Section: The Eighth and Final Proof — Why the Body Cools Gradually at Death, and the Eightfold Argument Concludes

items.zh: 謂臨終時，或從上身分，識漸捨離，冷觸漸起；或從下身分。非彼意識，有時不轉。故知唯有阿賴耶識能執持身。此若捨離，即於身分冷觸可得，身無覺受。意識不爾。是故若無阿賴耶識，不應道理。
items.en:
Second, explaining; first, distinguishing this from mere interruption. At the time of death, whether from the upper or lower portion of the body, consciousness gradually withdraws, and a sensation of coldness gradually arises accordingly; this is not the mental consciousness, which has at times already ceased.
Second, presenting what is capable of sustaining. Therefore it is known that only the store-consciousness can sustain the body; when it withdraws, coldness is found in the corresponding part of the body, with no sensation remaining. The mental consciousness is not like this.
Third, concluding. Therefore, apart from the store-consciousness, this does not make sense.

items.title: Section: Five Aspects of the Store-Consciousness — Four Building Saṃsāra's Turning, One Building Its Reversal

items.zh: 復次，嗢拕南曰：所緣、若相應、更互為緣性、與識等俱轉、雜染污還滅。若略說阿賴耶識，由四種相建立流轉，由一種相建立還滅。云何四相建立流轉？當知建立所緣轉故，建立相應轉故，建立互為緣性轉故，建立識等俱轉轉故。云何一相建立還滅？謂由建立雜染轉故，及由建立彼還滅故。
items.en:
Third, the full, detailed explanation; first, clarifying establishment; first, the summary verse. Furthermore, the summary verse states: its object, correspondence, mutual causal relationship, co-arising with consciousness, and the turning and reversal of defilement.
Second, the prose; first, briefly distinguishing; first, stating. In brief, the store-consciousness is established through four aspects accounting for the turning of saṃsāra, and one aspect accounting for its reversal.
Second, distinguishing; first, establishing the turning. What four aspects establish the turning? Know that these are the establishment of its object, the establishment of its correspondence, the establishment of its mutual causal relationship, and the establishment of its co-arising with other consciousnesses.
Second, establishing reversal. What single aspect establishes reversal? The establishment of the turning of defilement, together with the establishment of that same defilement's own reversal.

items.zh: 云何建立所緣轉相？謂若略說，阿賴耶識由於

items.title: Section: A Lamp's Flame and Its Wick — How the Store-Consciousness Perceives Both Body and World at Once

items.zh: 二種所緣境轉。一、由了別內執受故；二、由了別外無分別器相故。了別內執受者，謂能了別遍計所執自性妄執習氣，及諸色根根所依處。此於有色界。若在無色，唯有習氣執受了別。了別外無分別器相者，謂能了別依止緣內執受阿賴耶識故，於一切時無有間斷器世間相。譬如燈焰生時，內執膏炷，外發光明；如是阿賴耶識緣內執受，緣外器相生起道理，應知亦爾。復次，阿賴耶識緣境微細，世聰慧者亦難了故。復次，阿賴耶識緣境無廢，時無變易。從初執受剎那乃至命終，一味了別而轉故。復次，阿賴耶識於所緣境念念生滅，當知剎那相續流轉，非一非常。復次，阿賴耶識，當言於欲界中，緣狹小執受境；於色界中，緣廣大執受境；於無色界空無邊處、識無邊處，緣無量執受境；於無所有處，緣微細執受境；於非想非非想處，緣極微細執受境。如是了別二種所緣故，於所緣境微細了別故，相似了別故，剎那了別故，了別狹小執受所緣故，了別廣大執受所緣故，了別無量執受所緣故，了別微細執受所緣故，了別極微細執受所緣故，應知建立阿賴耶識所緣轉相。
items.en:
Second, in the formless realm. In the formless realm, there is only cognition of habitual traces as appropriated.
Second, cognizing the external, non-discriminated appearance of the environment; first, stating this characteristic. Cognizing the external, non-discriminated appearance of the environment means cognizing, in dependence on the very store-consciousness that cognizes internal appropriation, the appearance of the physical environment without interruption at any time.
Second, the simile applied. Just as a lamp's flame, when it arises, simultaneously holds the wick and oil within while casting light outward, so too should the manner in which the store-consciousness cognizes internal appropriation and the external environment be understood.
Second, clarifying its subtlety. Furthermore, the store-consciousness's own cognizing of its object is subtle, difficult for even the intelligent of the world to understand.
Second, the differences in its manner of activity; first, similar cognition. Furthermore, the store-consciousness cognizes its object without cessation, unchanging over time, one uninterrupted flavour of cognizing from the very first moment of appropriation until death.
Second, momentary cognition. Furthermore, the store-consciousness's cognizing of its object arises and perishes moment by moment; know that it continues moment by moment, neither a single thing nor permanent.
Third, the differences across realms. Furthermore, it should be said that the store-consciousness cognizes a narrow object of appropriation in the desire realm, a vast object in the form realm, an immeasurable object in the sphere of infinite space and infinite consciousness, a subtle object in the sphere of nothing whatsoever, and a most subtle object in the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception.
Second, concluding the essential meaning. Through cognizing these two kinds of object, cognizing them subtly, through similar and momentary cognition, and cognizing objects narrow, vast, immeasurable, subtle, and most subtle — one should understand the establishment of the store-consciousness's own object.

items.title: Section: Five Mental Factors That Never Leave the Store-Consciousness's Side

items.zh: 云何建立相應轉相？謂阿賴耶識與五遍行心相應所恒共相應。謂作意、觸、受、想、思。如是五法亦唯異熟所攝，最極微細，世聰慧者亦難了故。亦常一類緣境而轉。又阿賴耶識相應受，一向不苦不樂，無記性攝。當知餘心法行相亦爾。如是遍行心所相應故，異熟一類相應故，極微細轉相應故，恒常一類緣境而轉相應故，不苦不樂相應故，一向無記相應故，應知建立阿賴耶識相應轉相。
items.en:
Second, the aspect of correspondence; first, posing the question. How is the aspect of correspondence established?
Second, explaining; first, listing the factors. The store-consciousness constantly corresponds with the five universal mental factors: attention, contact, feeling, perception, and volition.
Second, distinguishing their characteristics; first, belonging solely to ripened result and being exceedingly subtle. These five factors likewise belong solely to ripened result, exceedingly subtle, difficult for even the intelligent of the world to understand.
Second, constantly uniform in engaging their object. They also constantly engage their object in a uniform manner.
Third, corresponding with neutral, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling; first, presenting the corresponding feeling. Also, the feeling corresponding to the store-consciousness is invariably neither painful nor pleasant, belonging to the neutral category.
Second, extending this to the remaining mental factors. Know that the manner of activity of the remaining mental factors is likewise so.
Third, concluding the essential meaning. Through corresponding with the universal mental factors, through uniformly belonging to ripened result, through exceedingly subtle correspondence, through constant, uniform engagement with their object, through correspondence with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, and through uniformly neutral correspondence, one should understand the establishment of the store-consciousness's own correspondence.

blocks.text: The eight proofs end with the body cooling at death. Then the treatise describes the store-consciousness itself: what it perceives, and what accompanies it.

Such bodily sensations do occur, even in deep meditation. Master Cháng Bǎi: only because the store-consciousness holds the body can the three feelings be established. Environment and body belong to the store-consciousness, the sense of self to manas, objects to the six.

Master Cháng Bǎi: at that time the mental consciousness has no clarity, and it isn't always continuous, so it cannot sustain the body. (Untranslated, 0579c17: "Why would consciousness at death be unreasonable without the store-consciousness?")
"Four for turning, one for reversal": four describe how saṃsāra turns; one, how it is reversed.

"A lamp's flame holds wick and oil and casts light." Master Cháng Bǎi: inner holding is the wick; the environment is an object, not held. Formless beings have no faculties; only "traces" are cognised, and traces are seeds by another name. The scope: narrow in the desire realm, vast in the form realm, then immeasurable.

Invariably neither painful nor pleasant. Master Cháng Bǎi: because it continues similarly, beings cling to it as a self; yet moment by moment it differs and perishes, so it is neither one nor permanent.
"Neither one nor permanent." The store-consciousness is not a soul. It is a stream, and that is why it can be purified.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi assign the four cognitions?
options: environment and basis: store-consciousness; self: manas; object: the six
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: environment and basis belong to the store-consciousness, self to manas, objects to the six.

quiz.q: How do differences in bodily sensation prove the store-consciousness?
options: whether thinking or in concentration, the body feels many things; without it there should be none
quiz.why: Such sensations do occur. Master Cháng Bǎi: only because the store-consciousness appropriates the body can the three feelings be established.

quiz.q: Why isn't the gradual cold at death the work of the mental consciousness?
options: it has lost clarity and isn't continuous; only the store-consciousness sustains the body
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: at that time the mental consciousness has no clarity, and it isn't always continuous, so it cannot sustain the body.

quiz.q: How many aspects establish the store-consciousness?
options: four of turning, one of reversal
quiz.why: Four for turning, one for reversal.

quiz.q: "In the formless realm, only habitual traces." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain?
options: no faculties or supports; only traces, and traces is another name for seeds
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: formless beings have no faculties or supports; only traces are cognized, and traces are seeds by another name.

quiz.q: Which simile shows it cognizing inner and outer at once?
options: a lamp flame: holding wick and oil within, casting light without
quiz.why: A lamp's flame holds wick and oil and casts light. Master Cháng Bǎi: inner appropriation is the wick; the environment is an object, not appropriated.

quiz.q: What object of appropriation does it cognize in the desire and form realms?
quiz.why: Narrow in the desire realm, vast in the form realm, then immeasurable, subtle, most subtle.

quiz.q: The text says "one flavour" and also "moment by moment." How does Master Cháng Bǎi take them together?
options: similar continuity leads to self-grasping; yet moment-by-moment change means neither one nor permanent
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: because of similar continuity beings cling to self; yet moment by moment it differs and perishes, so it is neither one nor permanent.

quiz.q: The English renders 想 as "discernment." What is the trouble?
options: it collides with "discernment" for 決擇; notion or perception would be consistent
quiz.why: The term collides with the chapter's "Deciding Discernment" and with "notion" elsewhere. Master Cháng Bǎi: correspondence is with the mental factors and with neutral feeling.

quiz.q: Which feeling corresponds with it, of what nature?
options: always neither painful nor pleasant, neutral
quiz.why: Invariably neither painful nor pleasant, neutral.
